newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel intervenes to support basket.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel intervenes to support basket.

text.p: The Bank of Israel intervened twice in shekel trading, buying foreign currency to boost the basket of key currencies, dealers said.

"In early trading the central bank intervened on a low scale to raise the basket slightly. Towards the end of trading it intervened again, this time more aggressively," a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank said.
The representative rate for the basket was set at 3.5416 shekels against 3.5402 on Monday.
The basket is now 7.0 percent below the slope.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against the basket of currencies representing Israel's key trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.
The central bank does not confirm currency interventions.
